docs.text: Today's theme: Today's front page mixes AI and open-source tooling with deep concerns about privacy, platform accountability, and software supply chains.

docs.title: 📌 Suggested Reads
docs.text:
• Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation — Open-weights 3B moderation model is immediately testable on Hugging Face and valuable for multimodal content filtering.
  • FFmpeg 9.0 — Huge FFmpeg release with new encoders, filters, and muxing features—essential update for anyone doing video or audio tooling.
  • DeepSeek V4 Flash on a Single AMD MI300X — DeepSeek V4 Flash on MI300X is a useful data point for cheap AI inference, but read the hardware-cost caveat in the comments.
  • Harness engineering for self-improvement — Relevant to anyone building self-improving agents; the top comment highlights harness-task fit as the key design constraint.
  • Eight Myths on Software Engineering and GenAI — Directly engages with what GenAI does and doesn't change in software engineering, with a stage-by-stage breakdown in comments.
  • Show HN: Maple-Preview – Ternary 20B MoE running at 120 tok/s on a iPhone — Shows a 20B MoE model running at 120 tok/s on an iPhone—a striking milestone for on-device AI.
  • Show HN: Fine-tune an 8B model on a 4 GB laptop GPU — Practical technique for fine-tuning large models on low-VRAM laptops; the author's comment explains the key insight.
  • Keyv and friends compromised in active Shai-Hulud supply chain attack — Active npm supply-chain attack affecting popular packages; security teams should know the details.
  • DuckDB – Data power tools for your laptop, now in Clojure (2023) — DuckDB's Clojure ecosystem is maturing; commenters compare production libraries, so it's a good evaluation read for data engineers.

docs.title: All Stories
docs.text:
• AI-Generated Images Discourage Me from Reading Your Blog — The top comment notes that readers also scan for 'agent-written technical blog' structures, so generic AI images are just one of several AI-slop signals that push people away.
  • Show HN: Simple algorithm and color space to generate diverse skin tones — The top comment praises hands-on color-space projects like this, though it notes real work often goes in the opposite direction with heuristics like isGray and isCloseToWhite.
  • Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation — Mistral's 3B Shieldstral gives a compact open-weights option for text and image moderation, and the top comment simply links the Hugging Face page to get started.
  • FFmpeg 9.0 — FFmpeg 9.0's changelog highlights Playdate video encoding, LCEVC muxing, and a new v360_vulkan filter, making it a broad release for multimedia tooling.
  • Apple says more ex-employees may have taken confidential data to OpenAI — Apple's complaint reportedly expands to more former employees possibly leaking confidential data to OpenAI, but HN's top response is a bare 'Yes'—suggesting the update adds little new signal.
  • DeepSeek V4 Flash on a Single AMD MI300X — DeepSeek claims V4 Flash runs on a single MI300X, but the top comment notes AMD sells those only in roughly €250K eight-GPU boxes, so the 'single unit' premise is misleading.
  • Harness engineering for self-improvement — The top comment argues self-improvement systems need 'harness task fit'—matching the harness to observed behavior—rather than a one-size-fits-all setup.
  • AI fuels more than half of cybercrime in Africa as scams surge – Interpol — Interpol says AI is behind over half of African cybercrime, and commenters believe the real share is higher, noting how realistic AI scams hurt actual victims.
  • Eight Myths on Software Engineering and GenAI — The top comment's phase-by-phase table suggests 'writing code isn't the bottleneck' only sometimes holds; GenAI's value depends on contract, product, design, testing, and deploy stages.
  • Apple is getting this wrong — The top comment calls this a cherry-picked critique that doesn't address evidence in Apple's complaint, but concedes it casts doubt; so HN is split on Apple's position.
  • Web Security is Too Hard — The top comment's main takeaway is that Cloudflare looks incompetent rather than that security is inherently too hard, shifting blame from a systemic problem to one vendor.
  • Show HN: Maple-Preview – Ternary 20B MoE running at 120 tok/s on a iPhone — Maple-Preview's 120 tok/s on an iPhone is notable because it's a 20B ternary MoE, showing on-device inference is advancing past small dense models; the top comment simply says 'cool'.
  • You don't need React: creating a minimal UI library in Vanilla JavaScript — The vanilla-JS tic-tac-toe example convinced the top commenter they still need React, undercutting the article's minimalism pitch.
  • Show HN: Fine-tune an 8B model on a 4 GB laptop GPU — The author explains that during LoRA the frozen base model doesn't need to live in VRAM, which is how an 8B fine-tune can fit on a 4 GB laptop GPU.
  • Xbox goes down. You can't play games you own on disc — The outage blocks even disc-based games because of online ownership checks, and the top comment worries younger players are being taught that ownership doesn't exist.
  • Pi's Minimalism Is Its Advantage — The top comment found a pi config customized for side projects needed tweaks at work, showing that harness behavior is highly use-case-dependent.
  • How to Make a Nintendo 64 Game in 2026 — A 2026 N64 homebrew guide spotlighting Pyrite64 got the top commenter excited to try it, indicating classic-console development still has an active scene.
  • Thanks FedEx, This Is Why We Keep Getting Phished (2024) — FedEx's phishing-prone delivery emails raise the question in the top comment whether the software was built in-house or by consultants, pointing to UX ownership.
  • Waymo in Dallas — Waymo's Dallas launch excludes freeways, and the top comment asks whether 'all of Dallas' actually includes suburbs—so coverage is more limited than the announcement suggests.
  • libexpat now funded by the City of Munich for up to 6 months — The City of Munich is paying for libexpat maintenance through its Open Source Sabbatical program, a notable example of public-sector funding for critical open-source infrastructure.
  • I am retiring from fulltime writing (& pseudonymity) to launch Guardian Angel — Gwern appears to be leaving full-time pseudonymous writing for a new 'Guardian Angel' project, and the top comment notes his posts are now follower-protected.
  • Oxide Computer raises $445M (SEC Form D) — Oxide raised $445M but the top comment doubts whether it actually ships hardware, having never seen images or user deployments.
  • Keyv and friends compromised in active Shai-Hulud supply chain attack — The Shai-Hulud attack on Keyv and related npm packages prompts a top comment asking GitHub to proactively lock accounts that upload obviously malicious code.
  • Online ad giant Adform was hacked, proving once again why ad blockers are needed — The Adform breach reinforces to HN that ad-tech is a tempting attack surface, with the top comment saying anyone who's dealt with popups already knows why blockers are necessary.
  • Why some people mow a lawn better than others — The top comment says optimizing mowing as a graph puzzle misses the cost of turning, which is why the best lawn path depends on real-world maneuverability.
  • We finally learned to center a div, then browsers added sidebars — CSS centering is finally solved but new sidebar layout features bring fresh complexity, and the top comment jokes 'centering a div? Impossible.'
  • IP and DNS Leaks in WebKit Affecting Proxy Browsers and iCloud Private Relay — WebKit leaks can expose proxy users' IPs and DNS, and the top comment asks Apple for CLI controls over iCloud Private Relay and DNS-over-HTTP.
  • "Clean" Code, Horrible Performance (2023) — This resurfaced 2023 article argues clean-code abstractions can wreck performance, and the top comment simply notes its age, so the debate is familiar territory.
  • NHS apologises and admits Palantir have access to identifiable patient data — The NHS admits Palantir has identifiable patient data, and the top comment sees it as an irreversible done deal.
  • DuckDB – Data power tools for your laptop, now in Clojure (2023) — Commenters are using DuckDB-related Clojure libraries like tmducken in production and are now evaluating ducktape, making this a practical data-tooling thread.
  • How Cops Are Trying to Hide Their Use of Flock — The top comment compares police efforts to hide Flock use to the Gestapo and says most officers should be fired, reflecting deep distrust of automated surveillance.
